method.tool: coverage_search.py (--regex --whole-words, eight term sets in search/C11/terms.txt) was launched for all eight sub-questions (run.sh); under host load from parallel cluster runs it had not returned JSON by the time this map was assembled, so the LOADED layer rests on (a) an independent front-matter grep of every record with the same regexes (recgrep.py -> recgrep.json) and (b) targeted in-context greps of the files mapped to each world in cic/corpus-map (tgrep.py), with file and line for every cited hit. If the tool JSONs land later they sit beside this file under search/C11/S*-*.json and should be read as a check, not a replacement.
method.record_check: recgrep.py over records/*/*/*.md front matter (quote text/modern_rendering/retrieve_when; witness/term/gravity/force/story/demo fields; honest_limit/contested_claim/absence-source fields)
method.verification: verify.py: 25 quote records cited as RENDERED were re-searched verbatim in the vendored file named by their source record (normalised; variants exact / hyphen-joined / section-number-dropped / spacing-only)
method.layers: RENDERED = a record speaks to the sub-question (partial = a record answers only part of it or only as a guard); LOADED = a vendored file mapped to the world holds a passage read in context; IDENTIFIED = registered, unvendored; OTHER = outside the repo; NOTHING. Shared NPNF/ANF volumes yield other authors' hits (noted per cell).
method.tool_runs: coverage_search.py --regex --whole-words --max-source-hits 8, eight term sets (search/C11/S1-jews.json ... S8-rivals.json, re-run 2026-10-26; all exit 0). Used as a cross-check: for every world and old term set the tool's record class was compared with this map; no rendered record was found that the map lacked. Cells where the tool shows a QUOTE or WITNESS class but the map says LOADED or NOTHING are single-word false hits (reasonably, one way, outside the church, Saracens, Socrates the historian), read and discarded. Sub-question ids follow repo/07-subquestions.yaml; the eight term sets are grouped differently (S2 Jewish practice, S3 pagans, S4 philosophy, S5 Muslims, S6 saved-outside, S7 convert, S8 rivals) and were remapped to the fixed ids.

jewish_visitor._scope: C11.S1 'I'm Jewish, what would you have said to my face' (C11-16, with C11-05, 06, 11, 12). Records only; no Representative answer is written. 'Guard' = the record's use_note.not_for. Hostile vendored text = Jew-hostile passages in files mapped to the world (cic/corpus-map), cited by file and line; shared volumes can carry another author's words.
jewish_visitor._premise_correction: alx has no anti-Jewish polemic record. Every alx record that names Jews or Hebrews is listed below (6 files: clement-schoolmaster, christological-reading, septuagint-inheritance, philonic-inheritance, allegoria, christ). Only syr holds a polemic record (syr.term.anti-jewish-polemic and two Aphrahat quotes).

alx.guard_holds: Partly. Nothing hostile is rendered. But no not_for names the supersession reading, and the schoolmaster quote retrieves on 'whether people outside the church had anything true', so a Jewish visitor can reach it.
alx.wrong_if_bare: Schoolmaster quote: 'as the law [was] to the Hebrews' tells the visitor the Law was a custodian that has done its work, in the voice's own mouth, with no marker that this is Clement's view and the view of one side. Christological-reading: 'what makes Christian interpretation different from Jewish interpretation' invites 'Jews read the same text without Christ'.

npnf204 Athanasius, line 36486: 'the malice of the Jews who slew the Lord'
npnf201 Eusebius (799 Jew-term lines) and anf07 (47 hostile-word lines): not read through
alx.absent: Blame for the crucifixion, harm done, Jewish Christians (Origen on Ebionites, anf04 line 32864, is loaded only).

cappadocian.guard_holds: Yes. not_for: 'the cross-religious mourning as independently confirmed, when it is the encomiast's claim'.
cappadocian.wrong_if_bare: Without the guard: Jews grieving Basil would read as proof of good relations. With it the visitor still gets a flattering anecdote and no account of what the three said about Jews.
hostile_vendored: npnf205 Nyssa, line 3906 ('after the manner of the Jews'; 79 Jew lines not read)
npnf207 Nazianzen/Cyril of Jerusalem, 185 hits, not traced to author

desert.guard_holds: Not applicable: no record. desert.source.bell-jews-christians-egypt is a Melitian papyri edition (Jews in the title only).
desert.wrong_if_bare: Nothing to quote bare; the risk is the voice improvising.

npnf104 Augustine (412 Jew-term hits): line 5203 'the sevenfold penalty under which the Jews lie for the crucifixion of Christ'; line 5641 the Jews' preservation likened to Cain's mark. This is the Catholic side, not Donatist speech.
npnf211 (Sulpicius, Cassian; first hostile line 50138 'the unbelief of the Jews rejected'); salvian (12 Jew lines): not read in context

hal.guard_holds: No on the Oea story; yes on the quote. oea-tumult's not_for says it is not a neutral report. oea-gourd's text says the Jewish residents sided with the old version 'whether from ignorance or spite'; Augustine does write that (Ep. 71.5, npnf101 line 32546), but the story's not_for has no line against repeating it. The seventy-quote has no not_for on the Jews' own claim.
hal.wrong_if_bare: oea-gourd: the voice states, as the story's own words, that Jews acted from ignorance or spite, which is Augustine's guess about them. no-one-preferred: 'the Jews admit' Jerome's work is faithful, reported by Augustine, can sound like a Jewish endorsement.
hostile_vendored: npnf206 Jerome, line 8405 ('the Jews who blasphemed Christ'), line 32621 ('the Jews mocked God crucified'); Jerome's own contempt is not rendered
npnf102 City of God XVIII.43
hal.absent: The debt to named Jewish teachers is carried (the fluency contest); contempt, blame, harm are not.

ijc.guard_holds: Yes on the story ('no voice' for the Jewish community; Ambrose not principled; not corroborated). Open_Gaps ijc line 153 logs a safety-adjacent check. One blur: earlier-windows says 'our own bishop kept unpunished', while the story says the Callinicum bishop urged the burning and Ambrose of Milan shielded it. Leo's 'gentile' (guarded as non-Jew) is addressed to non-Jews and offers a Jewish visitor nothing.
ijc.wrong_if_bare: story: the visitor hears the harm owned, but the Jewish side only as a burned building. earlier-windows: the wrong bishop could be named.

syr.guard_holds: Yes, on every polemic record: no verdict on Jewish people or practice today, no invented Jewish reply, no invented Christian dissent, no claim that Jewish neighbours said what Aphrahat alleges. Gaps: frontier-plural-milieu ('a large Jewish community') and abgar-addai-legend (Tobia the Jew) have no Jewish-visitor guard but say nothing hostile.
syr.wrong_if_bare: Dem. XVII.1 alone: 'Jews who blaspheme the people gathered from among the Gentiles' sounds like a fact about what Jews did. Dem. XXI: an unnamed Jewish sage taunts the Christians and is called a blasphemer; the visitor hears the taunt only as Aphrahat retold it. sure-thing alone strips Jesus-is-God from its polemic frame.

witt.guard_holds: Yes on the 1543 treatise: disclosed at existence only, and not_for forbids narrating its content; the voice may not answer its later effect either way. Weak spot: the term.the-turk world_word says the Turk is 'named with pope and Jews as outside Christianity, one of the devil's instruments', and its not_for guards only the modern-political reading of 'the Turk'. AC XVII's 'certain Jewish opinions' is guarded as not naming who is ungodly.
witt.wrong_if_bare: what-we-have-never-settled: the visitor hears that a treatise against the Jews exists and nothing else; the 1523 'born a Jew' text, which would show the arc, is unvendored. the-turk bare: Jews filed under the devil's instruments.

witt.absent: Blame, harm done in the founder's own words; Jewish practice (Luther against the Sabbatarians is not registered).

findings: No vendored text in the Library is a Jewish voice: no Josephus, no rabbinic text, no Philo in cic/texts. Every Jewish voice a world can reach is a Christian's report of one (Aphrahat's sage, Augustine's Oea Jews). C11-02 (adding rabbis, Josephus) is a Library gap, not a records gap.

The Jewish visitor reaches records in only alx, cappadocian, hal, ijc, pahc, syr, witt. Syr's are the best guarded in the fleet. Three unguarded edges: hal.story.oea-gourd ('ignorance or spite'), alx.quote.clement-schoolmaster (supersession), witt.term.the-turk world_word (Jews as the devil's instruments). Five worlds have nothing (desert, don, gallic, lpc, rzg) while lpc and rzg map hostile text.

Muslims: only witt (a prayer against the Turk) and rzg (nothing) are in window; both map firsthand Ottoman material (Gerlach, Lucaris) that no record uses. Ten worlds are out of window and none says so.

Canon cells: no demonstration for f6-t-02 ('too narrow', C11-01) in any world, and none for f3-p-03 (temples and the old gods). Cappadocian has nothing on whether a good pagan is saved (C11-09) although its Open_Gaps already logs it.
